citation.sourceDocument: IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32 (2026 long-term capital gains brackets); IRC §1411 (Net Investment Income Tax)
citation.sourceNote: The preferential long-term capital gains rates are 0%, 15% and 20%, applied to a separate set of thresholds from the ordinary brackets. Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §2.02 gives the 2026 breakpoints as the maximum zero-rate and maximum 15%-rate amounts of TAXABLE INCOME: $98,900 and $613,700 married filing jointly or surviving spouse; $66,200 and $579,600 head of household; $49,450 and $306,850 married filing separately; $49,450 and $545,500 for all other individuals. Note the married-filing-separately 20% breakpoint is half the joint one while its zero-rate ceiling is half as well, and head of household gets its own pair — neither is a copy of single. The 3.8% Net Investment Income Tax (IRC §1411) stacks on top above $200,000 of modified AGI ($250,000 joint, $125,000 married filing separately); those thresholds are statutory and have never been indexed. Omitted at launch fidelity: the 28% collectibles rate, the 25% unrecaptured §1250 gain rate, §1202 qualified small business stock, and the interaction with the AMT. Verified against Rev. Proc. 2025-32 on 2026-08-29.
